# Drawing: Canvas, geometry and the display list

<!-- Generated by dist/sdk/gen-widget-docs.py from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

The one drawing trait, the shapes it uses, the recording canvas and the wire format.

## `canvas`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/canvas.rs`)

The `Canvas` trait: every call an app makes to draw. Two implementations here: [`crate::raster::RasterCanvas`] (pixels, through the
toolkit's `Gfx`: the device and the desktop window) and [`crate::list::ListCanvas`] (records a [`crate::list::DisplayList`]: a browser,
a client, a test, a WASM tile). An app written against this trait runs on both without a change.

### trait `Canvas`

```rust
pub trait Canvas
```

Methods:

- `fn size(&self) -> (f32, f32)`: The drawing area in logical units. Lay the screen out from this, never from a constant.
- `fn rect(&mut self, r: Rect, c: Color)`
- `fn rrect(&mut self, r: Rect, radius: f32, c: Color)`
- `fn outline(&mut self, r: Rect, radius: f32, width: f32, c: Color)`
- `fn line(&mut self, x0: f32, y0: f32, x1: f32, y1: f32, width: f32, c: Color)`
- `fn gradient(&mut self, r: Rect, top: Color, bottom: Color)`: A vertical gradient from `top` to `bottom`.
- `fn shadow(&mut self, r: Rect, radius: f32, spread: f32, c: Color)`: A soft glow around a rounded rectangle (a shadow when the colour is dark).
- `fn text(&mut self, x: f32, y: f32, size: f32, c: Color, s: &str, style: TextStyle) -> f32`: Text with its top-left at (x, y); returns the advance width.
- `fn measure(&mut self, size: f32, s: &str, style: TextStyle) -> f32`
- `fn clipped(&mut self, r: Rect, f: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut dyn Canvas))`: Everything `f` draws or registers is cut to `r`.
- `fn image(&mut self, _r: Rect, _img: &Image)  // has a default`: A picture stretched to `r` (keep the aspect yourself: see [`contain`]). A canvas that cannot draw it draws nothing; the default does.
- `fn set_type(&mut self, _o: crate::typeface::TextOpts)  // has a default`: How text is set from now on (family, letter spacing, tabular figures). The host sets it once a frame from the person's choices; a canvas that cannot honour part of it (the pixel canvas draws the person's family by itself) ignores that part.
- `fn type_opts(&self) -> crate::typeface::TextOpts  // has a default`: The type options now in force (so a replayed run can put them back).
- `fn blur(&mut self, _r: Rect, _radius: f32)  // has a default`: Blur what is already drawn inside `r` (the back of a glass surface). A canvas without blur ignores it.
- `fn path(&mut self, fill: Option<Color>, stroke: Option<(Color, f32)>, segs: &[Seg])  // has a default`: A shape of straight and curved segments, filled (non-zero winding) and/or stroked. The default draws the outline with `line` and the fill as thin horizontal bands, so a canvas that does not know paths still shows the shape; real canvases override it.
- `fn layer(&mut self, alpha: f32, f: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut dyn Canvas))`: Everything `f` draws is drawn at `alpha` (0 to 1) of its own opacity. The pixel canvas and the recording canvas scale every colour's alpha as it is drawn ([`AlphaCanvas`]); overlapping shapes of one group each fade, as a browser's `globalAlpha` does.
- `fn text_clusters(&mut self, x: f32, y: f32, size: f32, c: Color, s: &str, style: TextStyle, _advances: &[f32]) -> f32  // has a default`: A run whose clusters have the given advances (one per cluster, see [`path::clusters`]). A canvas that shapes text itself draws the run whole (the default); a recording canvas keeps the advances so a renderer without the font can place each cluster.
- `fn hit(&mut self, r: Rect, hit: Hit)`: A clickable region (also the accessibility tree: every control has a name and a role).

## `list`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/list.rs`)

The display list: what a frame is when it leaves the app for a browser, a client or a test. [`ListCanvas`] records it from `Canvas`
calls; [`DisplayList::replay`] draws it on any other `Canvas`; [`DisplayList::to_text`] / [`DisplayList::parse`] are the wire format
(plain text, one operation per line, versioned and additive: a list newer than [`DISPLAY_LIST_VERSION`] is refused by name, and an
operation this version does not know is an error naming the line, never silently skipped).

### const `DISPLAY_LIST_VERSION`

The wire version of the display list. Additive changes only; a bump needs a fixture folder (CORE-COMPATIBILITY-DESIGN.md).
2 (alpha.5) adds `textx` (family, letter spacing, tabular figures of one run) and `blur`; a list that uses neither is still written as
version 1, so older readers keep reading what they could read.
3 (alpha.7) adds `path` (fill and stroke of straight and curved segments), `layer`/`endlayer` (opacity of a group) and `textc` (a run
with the advance of every cluster); a list that uses none of them is written as version 2 or 1 as before.

```rust
pub const DISPLAY_LIST_VERSION: u32 = 3
```

### const `MAX_OPS`

Limits of a list a reader accepts.

```rust
pub const MAX_OPS: usize = 100_000
```

### const `MAX_BYTES`

```rust
pub const MAX_BYTES: usize = 8 * 1024 * 1024
```

### const `MAX_NEST`

The deepest nesting of clips and layers together.

```rust
pub const MAX_NEST: usize = 64
```

### enum `Op`

```rust
pub enum Op
```

Variants:

- `Rect(Rect, Color)`
- `RoundRect(Rect, f32, Color)`
- `Outline(Rect, f32, f32, Color)`
- `Line([f32; 4], f32, Color)`
- `Gradient(Rect, Color, Color)`
- `Shadow(Rect, f32, f32, Color)`
- `Text { x: f32, y: f32, size: f32, color: Color, style: TextStyle, text: String }`
- `TextEx { x: f32, y: f32, size: f32, color: Color, style: TextStyle, text: String, opts: TextOpts }`: Version 2: a run set with the person's family, letter spacing and tabular figures.
- `Blur(Rect, f32)`: Version 2: blur what is drawn so far inside the rectangle.
- `Path { fill: Option<Color>, stroke: Option<(Color, f32)>, segs: Vec<Seg> }`: Version 3: a shape of straight and curved segments, filled (non-zero winding) and/or stroked.
- `PushLayer(f32)`: Version 3: everything up to the matching `PopLayer` is drawn at this opacity (0 to 1).
- `PopLayer`
- `TextC { x: f32, y: f32, size: f32, color: Color, style: TextStyle, text: String, opts: TextOpts, advances: Vec<f32> }`: Version 3: a run with the advance of each cluster (a letter with its marks), so a renderer without the font places the clusters where the device's text shaper did. `advances` has one entry per cluster of `text`.
- `PushClip(Rect)`
- `PopClip`
- `Hit(Rect, Hit)`
- `Image(Rect, Image)`: A picture (F-SDK-164): `image X Y W H FORMAT PIXELS_W PIXELS_H SEQ BASE64`. Additive in version 1.


Public fields:

Methods:

- `pub fn a11y(&self) -> Vec<A11yNode>`: The accessibility tree, in drawing order.

- `pub fn translated(&self, dx: f32, dy: f32, action_base: u32, action_cap: u32) -> DisplayList`: The same list moved by (`dx`, `dy`) with every hit region's action raised by `action_base`; a hit whose action is `action_cap` or more is dropped (the drawing stays). An app that embeds a list made by someone else (the core's browser frame) uses it to put the picture inside its own layout without its actions clashing with its own.
- `pub fn replay(&self, c: &mut dyn Canvas)`: Draw this list on another canvas (the pixel canvas of the device, or a test canvas).
- `pub fn to_text(&self) -> String`
- `pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<DisplayList, String>`

### struct `AdvanceTable`

A text measure a client can have without a font file: the advance of each letter, as the page's own fonts drew it at a reference size,
scaled to the size asked (text widths grow in a straight line with the size). A letter the table does not know is measured like
[`approx_measure`]; a measure from a table is what makes a client (a browser tile, the engine) wrap and fit text as the device does.

```rust
pub struct AdvanceTable
```

Methods:

- `pub fn new() -> AdvanceTable`
- `pub fn put(&mut self, style: TextStyle, c: char, size: f32, advance: f32)`: Record that `c` is `advance` wide when set at `size`. A size or advance that is not a positive finite number is ignored.
- `pub fn len(&self) -> usize`
- `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`
- `pub fn width(&self, size: f32, s: &str, style: TextStyle) -> f32`: The width of `s` (a letter the table does not have counts as the fixed estimate).
- `pub fn into_measure(self) -> Box<dyn FnMut(f32, &str, TextStyle) -> f32>`: The measure to hand to [`ListCanvas::with_measure`].

## `path`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/path.rs`)

Paths and text clusters for the display list (version 3). Plain Rust with no pixel toolkit, so the client engine links it.

A [`Seg`] list is a path: `M x:y`, `L x:y`, `Q cx:cy x:y`, `C c1x:c1y c2x:c2y x:y`, `Z`. The wire form is the commands joined with `;`
(`M0:0;L10:0;Q10:10:0:10;Z`). Every renderer flattens with [`flatten`] and fills with [`fill_mask`] or strokes with [`stroke_mask`], so
the pixel canvas, the engine and the tile adapter agree on the shape.

### const `MAX_SEGS`

The most segments one path carries, and the most points a flattened path may have (a reader refuses more).

```rust
pub const MAX_SEGS: usize = 2048
```

### const `MAX_POINTS`

```rust
pub const MAX_POINTS: usize = 16_384
```

Coverage (0 to 1) of the filled shape for the pixels of a box: `(x0, y0)` is the box's top-left pixel, `w` by `h` pixels, row after
row. Non-zero winding, four sub-rows a pixel and exact horizontal coverage. Every subpath is closed for filling.


Coverage of the outline: every straight piece is a line of `width` with round ends (the union, as the `line` operation draws one).


## `raster`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/raster.rs`)

The pixel canvas: `Canvas` over the toolkit's `Gfx` (the device screen, the desktop window, the emulator's PNG). Logical units are
multiplied by `scale` on the way in, so an app lays out in logical units and the screen's size factor is only applied here.
A clickable region becomes a `Gfx` hit with `Event::Row(action)`: the adapter turns that event back into `UiEvent::Action`.

### struct `RasterCanvas`

```rust
pub struct RasterCanvas<'a>
```

Methods:

- `pub fn new(g: &'a mut Gfx, area: R, scale: f32) -> RasterCanvas<'a>`: Draw into `area` (pixels) of `g` with `scale` pixels per logical unit.

## `wire`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/wire.rs`)

The input lines a browser or client sends back, and the session that applies them. The renderer (`ui/displaylist.js`) writes exactly
these lines; a [`Session`] reads them, drives the app through the same [`Host`] every target uses, and answers with the next frame
as display list text. Plain text, one event per line, additive like the display list: an unknown line is an error that names it.

```text
ptr ID PHASE X Y T       pointer (PHASE is down, move, up or cancel; T in milliseconds)
key NAME                 enter backspace delete esc tab up down left right
key char C               one typed character (C escaped like the text of a display list)
text S                   typed, pasted or composed text for the focused field
action N                 a hit region was used (a screen reader's click, Enter on a focused control)
wheel N                  positive = towards older content
resize W H               the pane changed size (logical units)
tick T                   the heartbeat (T in milliseconds)
```
